name: Samuel
description: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy

points: When the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, she bare a son and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord. Samuel means asked of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: And the child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. So the priests were not seeing visions. He said there was no open vision.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: So Samuel finally said, yes, Lord, I'm here. I hear you. That was an inner hearing, a spiritual hearing. It was no voice uttering, but he heard it in here. That's his conscience. Watch this real quick. Go to 1 Kings 19, 19 and 10.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

points: And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went and lay down. And the Lord called yet again, Samuel. And Samuel arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And he answered, I called not, my son; lie down again.

A lot of you all are weak with your kids, and you will let your kids destroy your house. He restrained them not. He did not correct them. Some of you all get mad when we tell you all about your children and we tell you about your family, and you feel like we are picking on you. Here goes Eli the priest. God is complaining to a new priest, Samuel, that he is raising up: I am going to do something real bad to Eli's house, because I talked to him and he is not listening. It is the same thing in here. We will see things spiritually and tell you, your son ain't right, your daughter ain't right, your wife ain't right, and you yes us to death and overlook it like Eli, like you cannot get touched.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Remember, Samuel's mom, Hannah, sent him to the priest with priestly clothing as a little kid. Samuel is a grown man now. And it took him a while to be a part of the priesthood for God to start dealing directly with him in an exclusive place, like he did with Moses.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel?

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. And the Lord called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child. So Samuel kept thinking that Eli was calling him. No, it was the Lord calling him. So Eli the priest said, the Most High is dealing with him.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place. And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us.
Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end.

What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house. Because he warned Eli, his sons were wicked. So now he is telling Samuel, I am about to destroy Eli.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. He was scared to tell him what the Lord had just revealed to him.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. So he is ready to die because he did not correct his kids. He said, this is of God, just let him do it. I would have given my sons an exclusive whooping after I heard what Samuel said. You just heard from another priest, your God is about to tear your house up. So this was just crazy to me when I read it, when he already was speaking to Eli and he would not listen. Then he told Samuel, look, I am going to go and do this to him. And then Samuel was scared to tell him what he heard. The Most High will deal with men exclusively, in a place where he does not deal with somebody else the same way.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass.

That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: The word of Samuel came to all Israel, and Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, pitching beside Ebenezer while the Philistines pitched in Aphek. The Philistines never wanted to leave Israel alone.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

points: Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel: If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines. Go back to how we lost the battle even with the ark of God among us: we had strange gods among us. Deliverance is not just having the ark, it is applying the commandments that are in the ark, thou shalt have no other gods before me.

Who is Ashtoreth? Astaroth in demonology is a chief figure of hell, named after the Near Eastern goddess Astarte, and Astarte is the Hellenized form of Ashtoreth, a form of Ishtar, the goddess called the queen of heaven, associated with love, beauty, sex, and war. Samuel was exhorting the people to depart from these fake gods and goddesses of the nations, and to this day there are Israelites that have not put away Ashtoreth from among them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the Lord. They gathered, drew water and poured it out before the Lord, fasted that day, and said, We have sinned against the Lord; and Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpeh.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: When the lords of the Philistines heard Israel was gathered at Mizpeh, they came up against Israel again, and Israel was afraid. But this time, instead of running for the ark, the children of Israel charged Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines. They knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord, and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle, but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them, and they were smitten before Israel. That was no regular thunder; it was the Lord entering the battle himself. They had repented, put away the false gods, and the prayer of the righteous man reached his ears, so now the Philistines had to deal with the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: The Philistines were so terrified they put up no fight; the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh and pursued them, smiting them until they came under Beth-car. Then Samuel took a stone, set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel. As long as Samuel lived, the Lord kept them down.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

points: Christ gave the same picture: a nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and his citizens hated him. This is speaking about Christ; the same spirit that said set a king over us says, We will not have Christ to reign over us. When we read Samuel again, that is why the Lord said, they did not reject you, they have rejected me.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

points: Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay, but we will have a king over us, that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

points: Samuel heard all the words of the people and rehearsed them in the ears of the Lord, and the Lord said, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king; and Samuel sent every man unto his city.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

points: Saul thought he was going out to fetch his father's asses, but his purpose was to be led unto Samuel; the Lord had already told Samuel he was sending him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 9: Saul Is Led to Samuel the Seer

points: When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said unto him, Behold the man whom I spake to thee of; this same shall reign over my people. Saul was the man the Lord himself chose.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said unto him, Behold the man whom I spake to thee of; this same shall reign over my people.

note.label: 1 Samuel 9: Saul Is Led to Samuel the Seer

points: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the parlour and made them sit in the chiefest place among them that were bidden, about thirty persons, and had the cook set before Saul the shoulder which had been kept for him: unto this time hath it been kept for thee since I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 9: Saul Is Led to Samuel the Seer

points: Samuel communed with Saul upon the top of the house, and they arose early. As they were going down to the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us, but stand thou still a while, that I may shew thee the word of God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 9: Saul Is Led to Samuel the Seer

points: Going back: after chapter 9, Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head and kissed him: is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: When Saul had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart, and all those signs came to pass that day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: Saul's uncle asked him where they went and what Samuel said unto them. Saul told him plainly that the asses were found, but of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: Samuel said unto all the people, See ye him whom the Lord hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people; and all the people shouted, and said, God save the king.

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the Lord; and Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: He took a yoke of oxen and hewed them in pieces and sent them throughout all the coasts of Israel by the hands of messengers, saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the fear of the Lord fell on the people, and they came out with one consent.

note.label: 1 Samuel 11: Saul Delivers Jabeshgilead

points: The people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death. But Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the Lord hath wrought salvation in Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 11: Saul Delivers Jabeshgilead

points: At the end of chapter 11 Israel crowned Saul at Gilgal. Back in chapter 8 the people had pressured Samuel because they wanted to be like the nations round about them, and the Most High led him to choose Saul the son of Kish.

This is the aftermath speech. Samuel is putting it on record: I hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me and made a king over you; whatever happens from here came from what you asked for.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

points: So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

points: Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

points: Saul tarried seven days, but Samuel came not yet to Gilgal, and the people were scattered from him. And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering. Samuel was supposed to make the offering, not Saul. Not only was he bashful; that bashful spirit made him self-willed. You do your own thing, and when somebody checks you on it, you make excuses.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Samuel had instructed Saul in chapter 10: when you get to Gilgal, tarry seven days, make no moves until I arrive. Saul tarried seven days according to the set time, but Samuel came not at the moment expected, and the people were scattered from him and acting frantic.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: As soon as he had made an end of offering, behold, Samuel came. And Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him. When you are dead wrong and you try to cover it up, you meet him over there before he gets to where you messed up; you deflect and maneuver around. That is what brothers do.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and he offered the burnt offering, and Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel's office. And it came to pass that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came. He was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: Samuel asks, What hast thou done? Saul answers with excuses: the people were scattered from me, thou camest not within the days appointed, the Philistines gathered at Michmash, so I forced myself and offered a burnt offering. This is part of Saul's pattern of behavior; he never wants to hold himself accountable, he always deflects onto whoever else.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Samuel does not entertain the excuses: thou hast done foolishly; thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God. Saul thought he was only bending Samuel's word, but disobeying the instruction was disobeying the commandment of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: Samuel went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin, and Saul numbered the people present with him, about six hundred men. The Philistines encamped in Michmash, and the spoilers came out of their camp in three companies, toward Ophrah, toward Bethhoron, and toward the border overlooking the valley of Zeboim; three raiding parties sent out to invade Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: Samuel also said unto Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Then said Samuel, bring ye hither to me Agag. And Agag came unto him delicately, and said, surely the bitterness of death is past. And Samuel said, as thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. Samuel followed instructions; Saul played games. Remember Agag; he comes back up in this class.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Samuel said unto Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people; now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord. Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way when he came up from Egypt. Generations after the wilderness, the Most High still remembers; the generation of Amalekites had returned, and it was time to fulfil what was written.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Then came the word of the Lord unto Samuel: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king, for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. Mark the language: Saul did most of what was said, yet the Lord counts it as turning back and not performing his commandments at all.
And it grieved Samuel, and he cried unto the Lord all night. Pride had to be in operation for Saul to transgress on that level, and pride is where the throne is lost.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Samuel rose early to meet Saul, and it was told him that Saul came to Carmel and set him up a place, a monument to himself, and is gone down to Gilgal. When your transgression becomes the lesson, be thankful when the correction comes quietly and nobody knows your name; do not take the spirit of bitterness, because you deserved a lot more.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Saul greets Samuel first with a cover: Blessed be thou of the Lord: I have performed the commandment of the Lord. The first thing out of his mouth is a fabrication, knowing full well he transgressed.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Samuel answers, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear? If you performed the commandment, why do I hear animals?

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the Lord anointed thee king over Israel?

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: In this chapter the Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites and everything they have, and he did not do it. Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel? When you thought you were a nobody, the Lord anointed you king over all Israel.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Samuel said, Stay, and I will tell thee what the Lord hath said to me this night. When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the Lord anointed thee king over Israel? Samuel brings Saul back to his remembrance: when you thought nothing of yourself, with no confidence to be a ruler, the Most High still chose you.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord. Wait a second. Remember we read earlier in Corinthians about those that sinned and repented not. So Saul's initial response, was that a sign of godly sorrow? No. There was none involved.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Saul is in denial: Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites. Samuel breaks down the rebuke and Saul tells the prophet he is wrong.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Did Sirach not just say that the Lord did not have great delight in sacrifices and burnt offerings? Why is that? Because sometimes we will say, oh, for the multitude of my oblations the Lord is not going to remember my sins. For the multitude of my sacrifices the Lord is not going to remember my sins. Yes, he does. Why? Because there is no repentance involved. The repentance is being omitted, being left out. You are not going to the Lord being sorry for your sins. What you are doing is adding sins on top of sins.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Samuel makes it plain: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Samuel refuses: I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel. Think it through: Samuel gave Saul the opening at the bleating of the sheep, and Saul would not humble down; he asked why Saul disobeyed the voice of the Lord, and Saul justified himself again. Two admonitions were given and refused before this rejection.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou. So now I want to paint the picture. Saul is dealing with rebellion. Saul is dealing with disobedience. Saul is dealing with rejecting the Lord, putting forth the finger, playing the blame game. Now the Lord told the prophet Samuel, hey, let him know that I am choosing one of his neighbours, and someone that is better than him.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: As Samuel turned about to go away, Saul laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent. And Samuel said, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou. Just as Saul tore the hem of the garment, so the Lord tore the throne from him; and Samuel says this still before he has ever met David, the same word he gave in chapter 13.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: That is the spirit of vanity, caught up in a rank and a title while forgetting that the title came for pleasing the Lord; once you discontinue pleasing the Lord, the title is going to leave as well. So Samuel turned again after Saul, and Saul worshipped the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. Agag came unto him delicately, crouching and speaking softly, and Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately, and said, Surely the bitterness of death is past; with Saul under rebuke, Agag figured nobody was mad at the Amalekites anymore and he was safe.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. The old prophet did not play; he finished the commandment himself, measure for measure for what Amalek's sword had done.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah, and Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul, and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.

The mourning is what makes it sad: Samuel raised Saul up from nothing, saw his potential, and saw the Spirit come upon him in chapter 11 when he stood up as a savior for the people; he had hope in him, and it came to this. Samuel was grieved, and the Lord repented of the appointment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Recall the class on chapters 12 through 15: in chapter 15 Saul rebelled against the commandment, and after two admonitions he still would not humble down and repent, so the Most High rejected him from reigning over Israel and told him through Samuel that his kingdom would not continue.
Samuel had groomed Saul up and saw potential in the brother, so he mourned over him; the Most High asked how long he would keep crying over the man he had rejected.
Samuel is told to fill his horn with oil and go to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for the Most High had already provided himself a king from among Jesse's sons.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Samuel feared that Saul would kill him if he heard of it. Remember the influence and love Samuel had among the people; even so, this shows the power of the king. Saul raised no hand against Samuel yet, but a king had the authority to command a prophet's death.

The Most High told Samuel to go in with a heifer, as if coming only to sacrifice; he would go incognito, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul's replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Samuel did what the Most High spake and came to Bethlehem, and the elders of the town trembled at his coming and asked, Comest thou peaceably? Everybody knew Samuel did not play; if he was coming to your town it was probably for some judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: When Samuel looked on Eliab he judged through his own lens as a man: surely this is the Lord's anointed. The Most High corrected him: look not on his countenance or on the height of his stature, because I have refused him. Looking the mightiest and the tallest does not make a man the one the Most High picked.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, the older, bigger, more developed ones, and Samuel said of each, Neither hath the Lord chosen this; the Lord had not chosen any of these.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Asked whether these were all his children, Jesse answered that there remained yet the youngest, and behold, he keepeth the sheep. Samuel would not sit down until the young one was fetched. He was ruddy, of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to, a young handsome fella, and the Most High said, Arise, anoint him, for this is he.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: Samuel anointed David in the midst of his brethren, and the spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward, from that young age, being the youngest son.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

points: David fled and escaped and came to Samuel to Ramah and told him all that Saul had done, and he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth. David was smart: he ran to the prophet, into the tower of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: Saul sent messengers to take David, and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying and Samuel standing as appointed over them, the spirit of God was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied; a second and a third set of messengers were sent, and the same thing happened each time they entered that atmosphere.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: Then Saul went himself, fully set in his mind to take David's life himself, and the spirit of God came upon him also; he prophesied before Samuel, stripped off his clothes, and lay down naked all that day and all that night, wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets?

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: Samuel died, and all the Israelites gathered together and lamented him and buried him in his house at Ramah; and David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom

points: Samuel was dead, and Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. The Philistines gathered themselves together, and when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Saul turned to this because the Lord was departed from him and answered him no more, neither by prophets nor by dreams, so he had Samuel conjured up to tell him what to do.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy? Imagine that: the Lord is your enemy now, Saul. Because you were bashful, you were self-willed, you broke the commandments of the Lord, you were deceitful, you lied, you made excuses, you were easily manipulated. It all went back to Saul being bashful.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Saul fell straightway all along the earth, sore afraid because of the words of Samuel, and there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all the day nor all the night.

The chapter in sum: Saul inquired of the Lord and was not answered, so he turned to a woman with a familiar spirit and conjured up Samuel. Samuel told him that because of his disobedience the Lord was not dealing with him anymore, and prophesied that tomorrow Saul and his sons would be with him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: David and Samuel the seer ordained them in their set office, and they had the oversight of the gates on the east, west, north, and south, lodging round about the house of the Most High because the charge was upon them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The elders came to Hebron, David made a covenant with them before the Most High, and they anointed him king according to the word of the Most High by Samuel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The children of Israel present keep the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread seven days, and there was no Passover like it kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept such a Passover as Josiah kept in his eighteenth year.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among them that call upon His name, called upon the Most High and He answered them.
When Moses, Aaron, and Samuel called upon His name, they were keeping the commandments of the Most High. That is why they were answered.

note.label: Psalm 99: The Lord Reigneth, Let the People Tremble

points: Though Moses and Samuel stood before Him, the mind of the Most High could not be toward this people; He says cast them out of My sight.

note.label: Jeremiah 15: The Prophet's Burden

points: "Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days." All the prophets from Samuel onward foretold these days, tying back to the "you" who are the men of Israel established in verse 12.

cases.charge: Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth: telling Eli every whit and hiding nothing; and an accounting no man could contradict, whose ox have I taken?
cases.preview: Given to the Lord as a child, he served before Eli in days when the word of the Lord was precious and visions were rare.

cases.name: Joel and Abiah, the sons of Samuel
cases.charge: Turning aside after lucre, taking bribes, and perverting judgment in the seat of the judge
cases.preview: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel in Beersheba, and they did not follow his ways: they chased dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
